label: History
value: Anne Shirley is mistakenly sent to Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert
unit: Anne Shirley is mistakenly sent to Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables, who had intended to adopt a boy to help on the farm. Though Marilla initially plans to send her back, she and Matthew decide to keep her. Anne settles into Avonlea, forming an intense 'bosom' friendship with Diana Barry and entering school, where she breaks a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he calls her 'Carrots', sparking a lifelong academic rivalry. Over the years, Anne experiences various misadventures, such as unintentionally getting Diana drunk on currant wine, accidentally dyeing her hair green, and falling off a roof while walking a ridgepole on a dare. She forms a story club, participates in school concerts, and joins Miss Stacy's Queen's prep class. Upon entering Queen's Academy, she wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship. However, after Matthew suddenly dies of a heart attack and Marilla faces failing eyesight, Anne gives up her scholarship to stay at Green Gables, teach at Avonlea school, and care for Marilla, finally reconciling and making peace with Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned from Alberta.
unit: After returning from Alberta, Gilbert resumed his studies at Avonlea school in the fourth book. On his first day back, he teased Anne Shirley by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' leading to Anne smashing her slate over his head and harboring a long-standing grudge against him despite his immediate apology. Gilbert quickly established himself as Anne's chief academic rival. After completing his Entrance examinations, he attended Queen's Academy in Charlottetown to earn a First Class teacher's license in one year, where he won the Governor-General's Medal. Because his father could not afford to send him to college immediately, Gilbert planned to teach school to pay his own way. Upon learning that Anne wished to stay in Avonlea to care for Marilla following Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up his secured position at the Avonlea school so that Anne could teach there, accepting a post at White Sands instead. After this act of kindness, Anne stopped him on the road, and they finally forgave each other and became fast friends.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, unmarried life at Green Gables alongside his sister Marilla. Due to advancing age and heart trouble, he agreed to adopt a young orphan boy to assist with farm work, but drove to Bright River station to discover that an eleven-year-old girl, Anne Shirley, had been sent by mistake. Intrigued and charmed by her ceaseless chatter on the drive home, Matthew quietly insisted to Marilla that they keep her. Over the next four years, he continuously championed and spoiled Anne, giving her sweetmeats and secretly buying her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. When Anne won the prestigious Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy, Matthew expressed his deep pride in her. Shortly after her graduation, Matthew collapsed and died instantaneously at the threshold of Green Gables after reading a newspaper announcement detailing the catastrophic failure of the Abbey Bank, where all his savings were kept.

Intrigued and charmed by her ceaseless chatter on the drive home, Matthew quietly insisted to Marilla that they keep her. Over the next four years, he continuously championed and spoiled Anne, giving her sweetmeats and secretly buying her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. When Anne won the prestigious Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy, Matthew expressed his deep pride in her. Shortly after her graduation, Matthew collapsed and died instantaneously at the threshold of Green Gables after reading a newspaper announcement detailing the catastrophic failure of the Abbey Bank, where all his savings were kept.

unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of Avonlea school, where he frequently spent class time sitting with sixteen-year-old student Prissy Andrews to explain her lessons and write on her slate. During his tenure, he humiliated Anne Shirley on her first day by holding up her slate due to spelling errors, and later punished her for breaking a slate over Gilbert Blythe by forcing her to stand at the blackboard. On another occasion, after a sudden decision to punish latecomers, he singled out Anne and made her sit next to Gilbert Blythe, prompting Anne to quit school for several weeks. At the Debating Club concert in aid of the library, he recited Mark Antony's oration over the body of Caesar. At the end of June, he gave an affecting farewell speech with tears in his eyes as his time as schoolmaster ended.
